title: Number of Walsh characters equals $2^n$
statement: For each $n$, the number of subsets $S \subseteq [n]$ is exactly $2^n$. Since the Walsh characters $\chi_S$ are indexed by these subsets, there are precisely $2^n$ of them, matching the dimension of $L^2(\{0,1\}^n)$.
replaced:
There are exactly $2^n$ Walsh characters, matching the dimension of
$L^2(\{0,1\}^n)$.
